chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id altogether from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn 'Imran Al-Halbi from Abdullah ibn Miskan from Badr ibn Al-Walid Al-Khash'ami who said:

Yahya ibn Sabur came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to bid him farewell, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'By Allah, you are upon the Truth, and whoever opposes you is upon that which is not the Truth. By Allah, I have no doubt for you regarding Paradise, and I hope that Allah will delight your eyes [with the sight of victory/fulfillment] very soon.'

key_terms.لَعَلَى غَيْرِ الْحَقِّ: upon that which is not the Truth

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Sadiq say to Yahya ibn Sabur when he came to bid farewell?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s explicit endorsement of the Ahl al-Bayt’s followers, affirming their adherence to the Truth and contrasting them with their opponents. The Imam’s expression of certainty regarding their entry into Paradise, coupled with his hope for a 'near-term' fulfillment, reflects the Shia eschatological expectation of the reappearance (al-Zuhur) and the ultimate vindication of the faithful. This narration underscores the theological concept of 'Tawalla' (affinity with the Imams) as a guarantee of salvation.
